Physique refers to the overall shape, structure, and appearance of a person's body — particularly how it looks from the outside in terms of size, build, and muscular development.

When you talk about someone's physique, you are describing the visible, physical form of their body: whether they look lean, muscular, stocky, slim, broad, or anything in between.

A person's physique is made up of several visible qualities of the body:

  • Body shape and proportions — For example, wide shoulders and a narrow waist, or a stocky rectangular frame.
  • Muscle development — Whether the muscles are large and defined, or lean and subtle, or mostly absent.
  • Overall build — Whether a person looks heavyweight, lightweight, or somewhere in the middle.
  • Height in relation to the body — How tall or short a person appears alongside their frame.

All of these things together — when you look at a person and instantly form an impression of their body — that impression is of their physique.

This is equally important. Physique does not refer to:

  • A person's internal health — Blood pressure, heart health, lungs — none of that is physique. Physique is purely about outward appearance.
  • Facial features — A person's face is separate. Physique is about the body, not the face.
  • Skin color, hair, or clothing — These are not part of physique.
  • Fitness or stamina — Someone can look like they have a great physique but have poor endurance, and vice versa. Physique is about how the body looks, not how it performs. (Though, of course, the two often go together.)
  • A person's character or mind — Physique is purely physical.
The word has a slightly evaluative feel

"Physique" is often used when someone is assessing or admiring a body. It is a somewhat formal or deliberate word. You wouldn't casually say "he has a nice physique" in the same way you'd say "he has nice shoes" — it carries a slightly evaluative, often admiring weight. People use it most often when a body stands out in some way, whether for being very athletic, very powerful, or very lean.

This is different from just saying "body." Everyone has a body, but when you specifically say "physique," you are drawing attention to the notable qualities of that body.
Common contexts where the word is used

1. Sports and athletics:
Physique is very commonly used in sports commentary and fitness discussions.

  • "A gymnast needs a lean, compact physique."
  • "Swimmers tend to develop a V-shaped physique — broad shoulders, narrow hips."
  • "Wrestlers often have a powerful, stocky physique."

2. Fitness and bodybuilding:
In gyms and bodybuilding, "physique" is central vocabulary. People talk about "building a physique" meaning deliberately shaping their body through training and diet.

  • "He trained for two years to build an impressive physique."
  • "Her physique is the result of years of dedicated strength training."

3. General physical description:
The word is also used simply to describe what someone's body looks like, without any fitness context.

  • "Despite his age, he maintained a youthful, athletic physique."
  • "She had the physique of a dancer — long-limbed and graceful."

4. Formal writing and journalism:
You'll often see it in articles about athletes, models, or people whose bodies are professionally relevant.

  • "The actor transformed his physique for the role, gaining 20 pounds of muscle."
The range of physiques — how the word is modified

Because physique refers to the whole visible impression of a body, people describe it using adjectives that paint a picture:

  • Athletic physique — A body that looks trained, coordinated, and fit.
  • Muscular physique — A body with visibly developed, large muscles.
  • Lean physique — A body with low body fat and visible muscle definition, but not necessarily very large muscles.
  • Slender/slim physique — A body that is thin and lightly built.
  • Stocky physique — A body that is compact, short, and solid or heavy in build.
  • Powerful physique — A body that looks strong and imposing.
  • Average physique — A body that is neither notably muscular, slim, nor heavy — just typical.

Physique vs. figure:
The word figure is very similar and is often used interchangeably with physique, but there is a subtle cultural difference. "Figure" is traditionally used more in reference to women's bodies (especially their shape and curves), while "physique" is used more broadly and is especially common when talking about muscle, strength, and athletic build. That said, both words are used for people of any gender in modern usage.

Physique vs. body:
"Body" is the neutral, everyday word. "Physique" is more specific — it emphasizes the visual impression, the shape, and the state of development. Saying someone has "a great body" and saying they have "a great physique" are almost the same, but "physique" sounds slightly more analytical and formal.

Physique = the visible overall shape, size, and muscular development of a person's body.

It is the word you use when you want to describe how someone's body looks as a whole — not their face, not their health, not their personality. Just the outward, physical form of their body.
